candidate.change_summary: Revised the DIAL-012 candidate for all six independent Review findings: archive retry and five-minute candidate lifetime, fatal HLS error cleanup, cross-launch request invalidation, remote archive position restoration, seekable-range clamping, and stale media-key completion guards. Added remount-safe automatic pause deduplication with a bounded session marker and a 30-second freshness check.
decisions: Archive failure now preserves the selected episode and safe position, clears failed URL/HLS instance, and resolves afresh on Retry. Ordinary Pause retains a valid candidate until expiry or five-minute age.

Fatal hls.js errors are scoped to the current instance/source/attempt throughout playback; they release ownership and leave a retryable error. Position restore listens before attachment and also handles already-ready metadata.
View changes and model-visible launches supersede old picker/search/show callbacks, restore busy controls, and cancel pending automatic pause work.
Seek uses actual TimeRanges, including offset and disjoint ranges. External media-key completion checks attempt/source/abort immediately after claim and releases only its matching lock epoch.

Automatic pause request IDs are stored without media data in bounded sessionStorage. A remounted old card cannot repeat the request; when storage is unavailable or a card is older than 30 seconds, automatic pause fails closed and the visible Pause button remains usable.
tests: npm test passed 53/53 on the new candidate; TypeScript build and browser bundle succeeded.

Independent temporary reproductions /tmp/dial012-review-ui.mjs and /tmp/dial012-review-player.mjs now show NTS view/title retained after late country response, New launch retained after late search, resolver count 2 after archive error/Retry, and seek 0 clamped to range start 10.

New durable controller regressions cover failed URL retry, five-minute age, offset/disjoint seek ranges, remote Pause and saved position, expired HLS restoration when metadata fires synchronously, fatal HLS errors before/after manifest and stale-instance immunity, and delayed media-key claim after a new source starts.

Delivered UI regressions cover cross-launch country/search races and busy-state reset. A two-mount delivered-bundle test confirms an old pause card does not send Pause to a newly active owner, including after marker eviction when the old issuedAt has expired.
